notes.title: “On this rock I will build My church”
notes.intro: Jesus gives Simon the name Peter (Greek petros, “rock”) and promises him “the keys of the kingdom.” This is central to debates about church leadership.

views.label: Peter is the rock, and his successors the Popes continue his role
views.summary: Catholics understand Jesus to have made Peter the visible foundation and leader of the Church, a ministry continued by the Bishop of Rome.

views.label: The rock is Peter’s faith, shared by all bishops
views.summary: Orthodox Christians honour Peter as first among the apostles, but see the rock as the faith he confessed, held by all bishops; the Bishop of Rome had a primacy of honour, not universal authority.
views.source: St John Chrysostom, Homily 54 on Matthew; Orthodox teaching on primacy

views.label: The rock is Peter’s confession of Christ, or Christ himself
views.summary: Many Protestants read the rock as the truth Peter confessed (“You are the Christ”), or as Peter in his role as first preacher, without a continuing office of successors.
views.source: Treatise on the Power and Primacy of the Pope (1537), 25–29

notes.common: All agree Peter had a special role among the apostles and that the church is built on Christ.
